questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Digestion finishes in the stomach. Reteach point: Digestion does not end in the stomach: it continues in the small intestine, where most absorption happens.
questions.prompt: A student says digestion finishes in the stomach. What is the best correction?

questions.answer: Because digestion is completed in the small intestine and its villi absorb the digested nutrients into the blood.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names digestion finishing in the small intestine and the villi doing the absorbing.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the small intestine, not the stomach, is where food enters the blood.

questions.feedback: Fat releases about 37 kJ per gram, more than twice carbohydrate or protein at about 17 kJ per gram.
questions.prompt: Which nutrient releases the most energy per gram?

questions.answer: The small intestine: enzymes finish breaking down the food (or the villi absorb the digested nutrients into the blood).
questions.feedback: Credit the small intestine plus either finishing digestion or absorption through the villi.
questions.prompt: Name the organ food passes through immediately after the stomach, and one thing that happens there.
